title: De Quervain Tenosynovitis
qa: Which tendons are involved? Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis.
Why compare sides on the Eichhoff test? It can be painful in healthy people.
What splint is used? A thumb spica splint.
How do you advise a new mother? Lift with palms up, thumb tucked, and share lifting where possible.
What must be excluded after a fall? Scaphoid fracture.

fields.Position and action: The examiner grasps the patient's thumb and quickly deviates the hand toward the little finger side
fields.Positive: Sharp pain at the radial styloid

fields.Position and action: Patient makes a fist with the thumb inside; examiner moves the wrist into ulnar deviation
fields.Notes: Can be painful in healthy people; compare sides

tests.name: WHAT test (Wrist Hyperflexion and Abduction of the Thumb)

fields.Position and action: Wrist fully flexed, patient resists thumb abduction
fields.Notes: Reported to be more specific [Ref – to verify]

redFlags.Finding: Hot, red, swollen tendon sheath with fever

manualNotes: Thumb spica splint (wrist and thumb, interphalangeal joint free) for several weeks, especially during aggravating tasks [Ref – to verify].
Activity change: lift the baby with forearms supinated and the thumb close to the hand; avoid repeated pinch and wrist deviation.
Exercise: after pain settles, isometric then isotonic thumb extension and abduction, wrist radial deviation, grip. Manual therapy: limited role.
Medical: corticosteroid injection has good short-term evidence [Ref – to verify]; surgery for persistent cases.
